single-gpu-forward-backward.summary: Recover one training step from forward dependencies and reverse-mode order.
single-gpu-forward-backward.objective: Order attention, MLP, loss, backward, and the optimizer step.
teachingPoints: Backward starts at the scalar loss.
The optimizer can update parameters only after every required gradient is available.

implementationSketch.label: Displayed training dependency
implementationSketch.note: Gradient clearing and input loading are outside the displayed trace.

single-gpu-forward-backward.insight: Backward runs MLP before attention; the optimizer waits for both.
single-gpu-forward-backward.hint: Run forward through the loss, then reverse MLP and attention.
single-gpu-forward-backward.explanation: backward starts at the loss, visits MLP before attention, then releases the optimizer.

dependencies.label: Loss releases backward
dependencies.explanation: Reverse mode starts from the scalar loss, so MLP backward cannot begin before the loss exists.

dependencies.label: Gradients flow in reverse
dependencies.explanation: Attention backward consumes the activation gradient produced by MLP backward.

dependencies.label: Gradients gate the update
dependencies.explanation: The optimizer waits until the final parameter gradients have been produced.

concepts.definition: Propagate gradients from the scalar loss toward earlier operations in reverse dependency order.
One teaching block aggregates the kernels belonging to a complete attention or MLP sublayer.

single-gpu-moe.summary: Reconstruct the local sparse-MLP path around grouped GEMM.
single-gpu-moe.objective: Order the local MoE path from routing to weighted token restoration.
teachingPoints: Permutation is a local token-major to expert-major layout transform; it is not communication.
Routing weights are applied while expert outputs are scattered back to token order.

implementationSketch.label: Local MoE forward
implementationSketch.note: The router includes score normalization and top-k selection.

single-gpu-moe.insight: Grouped GEMM needs expert-major tokens. Its outputs must return to token order.
single-gpu-moe.hint: Expert-major input must exist before grouped GEMM; token order is restored afterward.
single-gpu-moe.explanation: tokens are grouped by expert for GEMM, then restored and weighted.

dependencies.label: Routes define the layout
dependencies.explanation: Top-k expert assignments are required before token copies can be grouped by expert.

dependencies.label: Expert layout gates GEMM
dependencies.explanation: Grouped GEMM expects contiguous expert-major token groups, not the original token order.

dependencies.label: Expert outputs restore tokens
dependencies.explanation: Outputs can be weighted and scattered back only after expert compute has finished.

concepts.definition: Apply many expert-specific matrices while allowing each expert to receive a different token count.
Weight expert outputs and scatter-add them to their original token positions.

moe-expert-parallel.summary: Insert expert dispatch and combine around a local MoE data path.
moe-expert-parallel.objective: Add dispatch and combine to the local MoE forward path.
teachingPoints: Dispatch sends routed activations to expert owners; combine returns expert outputs to token owners.
EP adds rank exchange but does not eliminate local permutation and unpermutation.

implementationSketch.label: Expert-parallel MoE forward
implementationSketch.note: TorchTitan performs both source routing order and destination-local expert grouping; the puzzle folds the latter into the expert block.

moe-expert-parallel.insight: EP moves activations between token owners and expert owners. Local permutation is still required.
moe-expert-parallel.hint: Dispatch consumes routed token groups. Combine cannot begin until expert outputs exist.
moe-expert-parallel.explanation: dispatch moves inputs to expert owners; combine returns outputs before token restoration.

dependencies.label: Packed tokens feed dispatch
dependencies.explanation: Dispatch needs the source-side routed token buffer before it can exchange activations.

dependencies.label: Split counts gate payload
dependencies.explanation: This measured implementation exchanges dynamic per-peer counts before launching the payload all-to-all.

dependencies.label: Expert outputs feed combine
dependencies.explanation: Combine cannot return activations to token owners until local expert compute has produced them.

concepts.definition: Send routed token activations to ranks that own the selected experts.
Per-peer message sizes determined by the current routing assignment.

moe-expert-parallel-backward.summary: Reverse expert-parallel combine and dispatch through grouped expert backward.
moe-expert-parallel-backward.objective: Order the EP backward path from dY exchange to dX return.
teachingPoints: Combine backward sends dY from token owners to expert owners, the same rank direction as forward dispatch.
Dispatch backward returns dX from expert owners to token owners, the same rank direction as forward combine.

implementationSketch.label: Expert-parallel MoE adjoints
implementationSketch.note: The two backward all-to-alls invert tensor ownership; they are not named after their forward rank direction.

moe-expert-parallel-backward.insight: Backward reverses both the local layout changes and tensor ownership.
moe-expert-parallel-backward.hint: Send dY toward expert owners first; return dX toward token owners last.
moe-expert-parallel-backward.explanation: dY moves to expert owners before local backward; dX returns to token owners afterward.

dependencies.label: dY returns to expert owners
dependencies.explanation: The backward of forward combine first moves output gradients from token owners back to expert owners.

dependencies.label: Expert-major dY gates backward
dependencies.explanation: Grouped expert backward needs output gradients restored to expert-major order.

dependencies.label: dX returns to token owners
dependencies.explanation: After local layout inversion, dispatch backward sends expert-input gradients back to their token-owner ranks.

concepts.definition: The adjoint of the collective that returned expert outputs to token owners.
The adjoint of the collective that sent expert inputs to expert owners.

tensor-parallel-dense.summary: Place replicated-residual TP reductions around one dense transformer layer.
tensor-parallel-dense.objective: Place the four all-reduces in one TP layer: two in forward and two in backward.
teachingPoints: Row-parallel forward produces partial outputs, so attention and MLP each end with an all-reduce.
Column-parallel backward produces partial input gradients, which are summed before RMSNorm backward.

implementationSketch.label: Replicated-residual TP layer
implementationSketch.note: Autograd produces matching input-gradient reductions for the two column-parallel projections.

tensor-parallel-dense.insight: Row-parallel forward outputs and column-parallel input gradients are partial and must be summed.
tensor-parallel-dense.hint: Find the partial output after each forward sublayer and the partial dX before each RMSNorm backward.
tensor-parallel-dense.explanation: the two forward outputs and two backward input gradients are reduced before their consumers.

dependencies.label: Partial attention output is reduced
dependencies.explanation: The row-parallel output projection produces only a partial residual contribution, so the residual path waits for the all-reduce.

dependencies.label: Partial MLP output is reduced
dependencies.explanation: The row-parallel down projection must be summed across TP ranks before the replicated residual is complete.

dependencies.label: Reconstructed dX gates norm
dependencies.explanation: RMSNorm backward consumes the complete residual gradient, so it waits for the column-parallel input-gradient all-reduce.

concepts.definition: Shard output features; forward is local, while backward input gradients are partial.
Shard input features; forward outputs are partial and must be summed.

tensor-sequence-parallel.summary: Reconstruct TP layout transitions with a sequence-sharded residual stream.
tensor-sequence-parallel.objective: Place the all-gather/reduce-scatter pair around attention and MLP in forward and backward.
teachingPoints: RMSNorm and residual operations stay sequence-sharded; TP compute consumes gathered token activations.
Autograd reverses each layout transition: output-gradient all-gather, local backward, input-gradient reduce-scatter.
tensor-sequence-parallel.insight: Sequence parallel keeps norms and residuals sharded; TP compute uses gathered activations.
tensor-sequence-parallel.hint: Forward gathers before compute and reduce-scatters afterward. Backward reverses those layout changes.
tensor-sequence-parallel.explanation: each sublayer crosses from sequence-sharded to gathered layout and back.

dependencies.label: Norm runs on the shard
dependencies.explanation: Sequence parallel keeps RMSNorm local to each token shard; only its output is gathered for TP attention.

dependencies.label: Gathered activations gate attention
dependencies.explanation: The TP attention projection cannot consume the complete token slice until the input all-gather finishes.

dependencies.label: Reduce-scatter restores the shard
dependencies.explanation: The partial attention output is reduced and returned to the sequence-sharded residual layout.

dependencies.label: Sharded dX gates norm backward
dependencies.explanation: Backward RMSNorm runs only after the TP input gradient has been reduce-scattered to the local sequence shard.

concepts.definition: Each TP rank retains only its token slice for norms, residuals, and elementwise work.
A collective that converts between sequence-sharded and TP-compute layouts.

tensor-parallel-async.summary: Schedule peer fetches against decomposed SwiGLU gate/up GEMMs.
tensor-parallel-async.objective: Interleave four activation chunks across two compute streams and the peer-copy stream.
teachingPoints: Async TP decomposes gather-plus-matmul so communication for one chunk can overlap compute on another.
Overlap is not automatically a speedup: decomposition, barriers, and lost fusion can cost more than the hidden transfer.

implementationSketch.label: Gather/matmul micro-pipeline
implementationSketch.note: Dependency pseudocode: TorchInductor emits the chunk GEMMs on alternating symmetric-memory streams.

tensor-parallel-async.insight: Async TP overlaps one chunk's transfer with another chunk's GEMM.
tensor-parallel-async.hint: Alternate chunk compute across the two streams while fetching the next remote chunk.
tensor-parallel-async.explanation: peer copies run beside chunk GEMMs, with a join before final SwiGLU.

dependencies.label: Fetch gates chunk 1
dependencies.explanation: Chunk 1 GEMMs can start as soon as that peer activation slice is available; later fetches continue concurrently.

dependencies.label: Fetch gates chunk 2
dependencies.explanation: Decomposition turns one full-tensor barrier into a sequence of smaller producer-consumer dependencies.

dependencies.label: The final chunk gates the join
dependencies.explanation: All gate/up chunk results must exist before the complete tensors can be joined.

dependencies.label: Joined tensors gate SwiGLU
dependencies.explanation: The elementwise SwiGLU activation consumes the complete gate and up projections, creating a final synchronization boundary.

concepts.definition: Peer-addressable buffers with corresponding layouts on every participating GPU.
Split one collective-plus-matmul dependency into smaller communication and compute waves.

fsdp-dense.summary: Schedule two dense layers with forward and backward FSDP prefetch.
fsdp-dense.objective: Place layer parameter all-gathers and gradient reduce-scatters around two-layer compute.
teachingPoints: Prefetch may start early, but a layer cannot compute until its own parameters are materialized.
A layer's reduce-scatter starts only after that layer's complete flat gradient is ready.

implementationSketch.label: Two-layer FSDP schedule
implementationSketch.note: With reshard-after-forward, backward materializes each layer's parameters again.

fsdp-dense.insight: Prefetch can start early; compute still waits for its layer's parameters.
fsdp-dense.hint: Overlap the next all-gather with current compute; reduce each layer only after its backward completes.
fsdp-dense.explanation: each prefetch begins early, while compute and reduce-scatter still wait for readiness.

dependencies.label: Layer 0 waits for parameters
dependencies.explanation: The first layer cannot start until its full parameter set has been materialized by FSDP.

dependencies.label: Prefetch hides layer 1 AG
dependencies.explanation: Layer 1 parameters are gathered during layer 0 compute and are ready before first use.

dependencies.label: Backward waits for weights
dependencies.explanation: Backward needs the layer weights again, so layer 1 MLP backward is gated by its backward all-gather.

dependencies.label: Complete gradients gate RS
dependencies.explanation: The layer-level reduce-scatter launches only after both MLP and attention gradients are complete.

concepts.definition: Materialize the next layer's parameters while the current layer computes.
Sum a complete flat gradient and retain one shard per FSDP rank.

fsdp-dense-granular.summary: Split FSDP units at attention/MLP boundaries to expose earlier gradient sharding.
fsdp-dense-granular.objective: Schedule all-gather and reduce-scatter for separate attention and MLP FSDP units in two layers.
teachingPoints: Finer wrapping changes gradient readiness, not the total parameter or gradient bytes.
MLP backward finishes before attention backward, allowing MLP reduce-scatter to overlap attention compute.

implementationSketch.label: Module-granular backward
implementationSketch.note: The asynchronous launch is what permits MLP gradient sharding to overlap attention backward.

fsdp-dense-granular.insight: Smaller FSDP units make gradients ready earlier, but add collectives.
fsdp-dense-granular.hint: Backward visits MLP before attention; release each unit's gradient as soon as it becomes complete.
fsdp-dense-granular.explanation: MLP reduce-scatter begins before attention backward finishes, creating earlier overlap.

dependencies.label: MLP waits for its own unit
dependencies.explanation: Separating FSDP units gives attention and MLP independent parameter-materialization boundaries.

dependencies.label: MLP gradients become ready first
dependencies.explanation: Once MLP backward completes, its smaller FSDP unit can reduce immediately while attention backward begins.

dependencies.label: Attention waits for its weights
dependencies.explanation: Attention backward remains independently gated by materialization of the attention FSDP unit.

dependencies.label: Attention gradients gate its RS
dependencies.explanation: The attention reduce-scatter cannot launch until the separate attention gradient is complete.

concepts.definition: A parameter group materialized by one all-gather and sharded by one reduce-scatter.
The earliest point when every gradient in an FSDP unit is available for reduction.

fsdp-moe.summary: Schedule dense and full-expert FSDP communication around a fixed two-layer MoE path.
fsdp-moe.objective: Place dense and expert all-gathers at first use, then reduce-scatters when each gradient is complete.
teachingPoints: EP=1 has no activation all-to-all, but each grouped expert GEMM still waits for the full expert FSDP unit to materialize.
Expert reduce-scatter starts only after the full expert gradient is packed and can serialize later dense reductions.

implementationSketch.label: Expert-FSDP without EP
implementationSketch.note: Expert prefetch may overlap attention and routing, but grouped GEMM waits for the gathered weights.

fsdp-moe.insight: EP=1 removes activation exchange, not expert parameter all-gathers.
fsdp-moe.hint: Local MoE compute is fixed. Place each all-gather before its first consumer and each reduce-scatter after its gradient pack.
fsdp-moe.explanation: dense and expert weights are gathered before use; gradients are scattered after packing.

dependencies.label: Expert AG creates a forward stall
dependencies.explanation: Attention and routing finish before the full expert weights arrive, so expert copy-out waits on the exposed all-gather tail.

dependencies.label: Expert AG creates a backward stall
dependencies.explanation: The local backward path reaches expert first use while the large expert-weight all-gather is still in flight.

dependencies.label: Packed expert gradients gate RS
dependencies.explanation: The expert reduce-scatter begins only after the complete flat expert gradient has been packed.

dependencies.label: Expert RS blocks dense RS
dependencies.explanation: The long expert reduction occupies the serialized FSDP reduction stream, delaying the already-ready dense reduction.

concepts.definition: Experts use an independent FSDP state so their large collectives can be scheduled separately.
Every rank can route to the complete expert set; no expert-ownership exchange occurs.

fsdp-moe-ep.summary: Schedule expert-FSDP communication where it meets the expert-parallel activation path.
fsdp-moe-ep.objective: Place the FSDP and EP communication that gates expert forward and backward.
teachingPoints: Grouped expert compute starts only after expert FSDP has materialized weights and EP has delivered expert-grouped activations.
Backward prefetch follows L1-before-L0 first use, while each expert reduce-scatter starts from its completed flat-gradient pack.

implementationSketch.label: Expert-FSDP + EP data path
implementationSketch.note: Dispatch can overlap expert-weight prefetch; grouped GEMM is the first operation that requires those weights.

fsdp-moe-ep.insight: Grouped expert GEMM waits for weights from FSDP and activations from EP.
fsdp-moe-ep.hint: In forward, join expert all-gather with dispatch before grouped GEMM. In backward, join expert all-gather with the dY exchange.
fsdp-moe-ep.explanation: expert GEMM begins only when routed activations and gathered weights are both ready.

dependencies.label: Expert weights gate SwiGLU
dependencies.explanation: Grouped expert compute needs the materialized expert weights supplied by expert FSDP.

dependencies.label: Dispatched activations gate SwiGLU
dependencies.explanation: The same grouped GEMM also waits for routed activations to arrive from token-owner ranks and be grouped locally.

dependencies.label: Unfinished AG exposes a stall
dependencies.explanation: Token-restore backward reaches expert first use before the expert weights are ready, so compute pauses until the all-gather completes.

dependencies.label: Expert gradients gate sharding
dependencies.explanation: Expert FSDP can reduce-scatter only after grouped backward has produced and packed the complete expert gradient.

concepts.definition: The number of ranks that shard the experts owned by one EP group.
Activation all-to-alls that move routed tokens to expert owners and outputs back to token owners.

ddp-terminal.summary: See why one terminal gradient bucket leaves communication fully exposed.
ddp-terminal.objective: Order backward, then place the only gradient all-reduce.
teachingPoints: DDP synchronizes gradients, not parameters; every rank retains a complete model replica.
A bucket can launch only after all parameter gradients assigned to it are ready. One model-sized bucket therefore waits for embedding backward.

implementationSketch.label: One terminal reducer bucket
implementationSketch.note: The optimizer is outside the measured window. A large reducer bucket is the real DDP analogue of terminal, unbucketed synchronization.

ddp-terminal.insight: With one model-sized bucket, communication waits for the last gradient.
ddp-terminal.hint: Reverse layer 1 before layer 0, finish the embedding gradient, then launch the only all-reduce.
ddp-terminal.explanation: the single bucket launches after embedding backward and remains exposed.

dependencies.label: Loss releases layer backward
dependencies.explanation: Autograd enters the last layer first and traverses its MLP before attention.

dependencies.label: Embedding gradient is last
dependencies.explanation: The model-sized reducer bucket remains incomplete until backward reaches the embedding parameters.

dependencies.label: The final gradient gates AR
dependencies.explanation: With one bucket, the only all-reduce cannot launch until every parameter gradient is present.

concepts.definition: Every DDP rank owns the complete parameters and computes gradients from a different local batch.
A flat buffer whose all-reduce launches only after every assigned parameter gradient is ready.

ddp-bucketed.summary: Place reducer buckets at their measured last-gradient readiness points.
ddp-bucketed.objective: Place each all-reduce where its bucket's final gradient becomes ready.
teachingPoints: Bucket order follows reverse-mode readiness; the 96 MiB cap is a construction target, so large parameters and grouping constraints can produce larger buckets.
Overlap shortens the tail, but concurrent NCCL contends with backward kernels for GPU and fabric resources.

implementationSketch.label: Bucketed DDP backward
implementationSketch.note: The benchmark registers PyTorch's default all-reduce hook only to record GradBucket composition; communication semantics are unchanged.

ddp-bucketed.insight: A bucket launches at its last gradient. Mixed-layer buckets can hold earlier gradients back.
ddp-bucketed.hint: Follow MLP gradients before attention. The cross-layer bucket waits for layer 0 down-projection gradients.
ddp-bucketed.explanation: each bucket launches when its final gradient is ready; NCCL follows that readiness order.

dependencies.label: The first bucket becomes ready inside MLP backward
dependencies.explanation: Its output and norm gradients are ready earlier, but the bucket launches only when the layer 1 down-projection gradient appears.

dependencies.label: One bucket crosses layers
dependencies.explanation: A layer 1 norm gradient waits for the layer 0 down-projection gradient that shares its reducer bucket.

dependencies.label: The last bucket forms the tail
dependencies.explanation: The embedding bucket cannot become ready until the final embedding gradient is produced, leaving a small exposed tail.

concepts.definition: The point when the final outstanding gradient assigned to one reducer bucket has been produced.
Communication and compute coincide in time but slow one another through shared-resource contention.

context-parallel-allgather.summary: Order partial attention when K/V is gathered once per call.
context-parallel-allgather.objective: Order partial attention by K/V owner, then place backward dK/dV returns.
teachingPoints: Local QKV, QK normalization, and RoPE complete before the first K/V collective begins.
Forward gathers K/V once; backward gathers K/V again but returns accumulated dK/dV cyclically.

implementationSketch.label: Native CP with all-gather rotation
implementationSketch.note: The remote iteration excludes the local K/V shard already consumed before the wait.

context-parallel-allgather.insight: One K/V all-gather feeds the remote attention steps; dK/dV returns one shard at a time.
context-parallel-allgather.hint: Follow K/V ownership from rank 0 to successive predecessor-owned shards.
context-parallel-allgather.explanation: local QKV runs first; gathered K/V shards feed remote attention in ring order.

dependencies.label: Local QKV gates exchange
dependencies.explanation: K/V cannot be gathered until the local projection has produced the rank-owned K/V shard.

dependencies.label: Gathered K/V gates remote attention
dependencies.explanation: Local-shard attention can run while the collective progresses, but the first remote-shard attention waits for gathered K/V.

dependencies.label: Backward gathers K/V again
dependencies.explanation: The remote partial-attention backward steps need the corresponding forward K/V shards before they can run.

dependencies.label: dK/dV returns to its owner
dependencies.explanation: Once the local partial backward produces a K/V-gradient contribution, cyclic exchange begins returning accumulated dK/dV to the owning rank.

concepts.definition: Combine partial attention outputs with log-sum-exp state without materializing the full score matrix.
Assign early and late causal sequence regions to each rank to reduce load imbalance.

context-parallel-alltoall.summary: Order partial attention with cyclic whole-shard K/V transfers.
context-parallel-alltoall.objective: Alternate partial attention with cyclic K/V transfers, then return dK/dV.
teachingPoints: Each transfer sends the current whole K/V shard to one neighbor; this is ring attention, not Ulysses head transposition.
Backward needs three K/V rotations to feed compute and four dK/dV rotations to return accumulated gradients.

implementationSketch.label: Native CP with cyclic all-to-all
implementationSketch.note: PyTorch launches the cyclic permutation before attention so transfer and partial attention can overlap.

context-parallel-alltoall.insight: Backward rotates K/V for compute and dK/dV for ownership return.
context-parallel-alltoall.hint: Track the owner of the K/V shard currently resident on rank 0.
context-parallel-alltoall.explanation: K/V rotates for each attention step; dK/dV rotates separately in backward.

dependencies.label: Local QKV gates rotation
dependencies.explanation: The first cyclic transfer cannot start until rank 0 has produced its local K/V shard.

dependencies.label: The next K/V shard gates attention
dependencies.explanation: The first remote partial-attention call consumes the K/V shard delivered by the first cyclic transfer.

dependencies.label: Rotation advances the ring
dependencies.explanation: Each partial-attention step waits for the next owner's K/V shard to arrive.

dependencies.label: Backward rotates K/V for compute
dependencies.explanation: Backward needs the same remote K/V ownership sequence before each partial-attention gradient step.

dependencies.label: dK/dV follows a separate ring
dependencies.explanation: K/V movement feeds backward compute, while a distinct cyclic exchange accumulates and returns dK/dV to the original owner.

concepts.definition: Send one whole shard to the next rank and receive one whole shard from the previous rank.
No sequence-to-head transpose occurs; each rank still executes one partial attention call per K/V shard.
